A quick guide for PTO editors

Keep the community in the loop.

Once your account has been connected, you can make everyday updates without coding or editing GitHub files.

1. Sign in

  1. Open PTO editor login at the bottom of the website.
  2. Choose Sign in to edit with GitHub, then sign in with your own approved account.
  3. If access is denied, ask the website administrator to check your invitation. PTO membership does not automatically give website editing access.

2. Update a page

  1. Choose Website pages, then select the page.
  2. Edit the clearly labeled fields. The preview shows how your draft will look.
  3. Choose Save to keep a draft. Your live website stays as it is.

3. Add an event or announcement

  1. Choose PTO events or News & announcements, then New.
  2. Enter the title, date, and details. Event times should be entered for Magnolia, Texas. For an all-day event, turn on All-day event.
  3. Add an optional link or approved image. Describe meaningful images in the image description field.
  4. Check the preview, then save your draft. Past events automatically leave the upcoming-events list.

4. Review and publish

Move a completed draft to In review or Ready. An authorized publisher reviews and publishes it. If publishing is blocked, your administrator may need to approve it first.

After publication, the website rebuilds automatically. Check the live page after the deployment finishes; publishing can take a few minutes.

5. Change images and links

Use the image field to upload an approved picture or choose an existing one. For the homepage, update the image, image description, and caption together. Keep temporary illustrations identified until they are replaced.

Membership, store, school, and contact links are under Site settings & links. Use complete links beginning with https://.

6. Restore earlier content

An administrator can open Content history & restoration, sign in, select an earlier revision, and create a restoration draft. Review the draft in GitHub and merge it to publish. This uses buttons rather than a code editor. The current website remains live until that draft is merged.

Restoration replaces page content, events, announcements, and uploaded images together with the selected revision. Review newer work before publishing the restoration.

A note about volunteering

The volunteer form prepares an email for the visitor to review and send. It does not collect a submitted form into a website inbox. Volunteer messages arrive at the PTO email address once the visitor sends them.
